item.title: HubSpot AEO vs. Profound: Features, pricing, and use cases
item.description: HubSpot AEO vs. Profound is a comparison between two answer engine optimization tools that take different approaches to AI search visibility. HubSpot AEO tracks how a brand appears in AI-generated answers and connects those insights directly to content creation and campaign execution inside the HubSpot ecosystem.
item.content:encoded:
HubSpot AEO vs. Profound is a comparison between two answer engine optimization tools that take different approaches to AI search visibility. HubSpot AEO tracks how a brand appears in AI-generated answers and connects those insights directly to content creation and campaign execution inside the HubSpot ecosystem.

Profound monitors AI visibility at greater depth, analyzing brand perception, citation sources, and competitive positioning across AI platforms. For most marketing leaders, SEO strategists, content teams, and RevOps buyers, the choice between them comes down to one operational question: does the team need faster insight-to-execution workflows, deeper AI visibility analysis, or both?

Why HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Is About Execution vs. Analysis

The question most marketing professionals face when evaluating AI search optimization tools is how to optimize for AI-generated answers. Specifically: does the team need a faster path from AI visibility insight to content and campaign execution, or does it need deeper analysis of how its brand is described, cited, and positioned across AI platforms?

That is the real distinction between HubSpot AEO and Profound. HubSpot AEO is an answer engine optimization tool designed to track AI visibility and help teams act on those insights inside the HubSpot ecosystem. Profound is an answer engine optimization platform focused on deeper AI visibility analysis, citation tracking, and brand perception monitoring.

Both serve legitimate needs. The difference lies in where the workflow ends.

For teams not ready to commit to either paid tool, the AEO Grader provides a free baseline for measuring AI search visibility before committing to ongoing optimization. It takes minutes to run and requires no subscription, making it the lowest-friction starting point in the category.

Pro tip: If the team has never measured its AI search visibility, start with the free AEO Grader. It generates a snapshot score across popular answer engines and takes less than five minutes to run. Use it before evaluating any paid tool.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Features and Core Differences

Both platforms track how a brand appears in AI-generated answers. The features that differ are the ones that matter most for how a team actually operates, such as how quickly it can act on what it finds, and how deeply it needs to understand why results look the way they do.

What is HubSpot AEO, and how does it work?

HubSpot AEO is HubSpot’s answer engine optimization product. It tracks how often a brand appears in AI-generated answers for a set of tracked prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. Then it surfaces prioritized recommendations to improve that visibility.

What distinguishes it from standalone monitoring tools is where the workflow goes after the insight is generated.

Because HubSpot AEO is built within the HubSpot platform, AI visibility data connects directly to CRM records, contact segments, and marketing workflows. A team can identify a prompt in which a competitor is outperforming their brand, see which customer segments the prompt is most relevant to, and move into content creation or campaign optimization without switching tools.

The HubSpot ecosystem—Marketing Hub for content publishing, Content Hubs for asset creation, and Smart CRM for audience context—enables recommendations to be meaningful rather than generic.

The free AEO Grader and HubSpot AEO are different products—one is a one-time diagnostic, and the other is an ongoing monitoring platform.

For teams building a broader answer engine optimization strategy, HubSpot AEO serves as the operational layer where visibility data translates into action.

What does Profound Track do, and where does it go deep?

Profound is an enterprise-focused answer engine optimization platform that measures how a brand shows up in AI answers, tracks visibility, share of voice, sentiment, and citations, and surfaces optimization opportunities. Where Profound differs is in the depth of that analysis.

Profound tracks a broader set of AI platforms than HubSpot AEO at the base edition, including Google AI Overviews and Claude, in addition to the major engines.

It offers flexible custom prompt tracking across topics and queries, advanced source and influence mapping that shows which domains shape AI responses, and brand perception analysis that goes beyond presence metrics to evaluate how AI systems actually describe a brand.

For teams that need to understand why they appear (or do not appear) in AI-generated answers, Profound provides more data to work with. The key trade-off is that Profound provides analysis but lacks a built-in execution layer for implementing improvements. Implementing improvements requires taking those insights into a separate CMS or marketing workflow.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Pricing and Plan Fit

HubSpot AEO offers a free AEO Grader with no subscription required. The standalone paid plan starts at $50 per month ($45 per month billed annually) and includes 25 tracked prompts with a 28-day free trial. Teams that want to connect AEO workflows to content creation and campaign execution within HubSpot will need Marketing Hub Professional, which starts at approximately $800 per month.

That step-up unlocks the full integration layer — CRM-informed recommendations, content workflows, and campaign triggers — and represents a meaningful upgrade over the standalone product.

Profound includes a free one-time AEO report as its entry point. Paid plans start at $99 per month ($82.50 per month billed annually) on the Starter edition and $399 per month ($332.50 per month billed annually). On the Growth/Standard tier, Enterprise pricing is custom. Agency plans are available from $99 per month.

For SMBs and mid-market teams evaluating AI search optimization tools on a budget, HubSpot AEO’s lower entry point and bundled ecosystem reduce the total number of tools required. For enterprise teams that already have a content operations stack and need Profound’s depth of analysis, the higher price point is justified by the data capabilities. Still, those teams should account for the additional tooling required to act on Profound’s recommendations.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Ease of Use and Adoption

HubSpot AEO is designed for marketing teams without technical expertise in AEO. Setup takes minutes: enter the brand, select prompts, and the platform begins tracking.

The dashboard surfaces visibility scores, competitor benchmarks, and prioritized recommendations in plain language, with guided workflows that move users from insight to action without requiring familiarity with how AI-generated answers work at a technical level.

This matters for cross-functional adoption when a content strategist, an SEO lead, and a RevOps manager all need to interpret the same data; a low learning curve reduces friction across teams.

Profound has a clean, modern interface, but it is built for users who are comfortable working with detailed visibility data. The platform rewards depth. Users who understand citation analysis, prompt-level tracking, and competitive share-of-voice metrics will get more out of it.

For teams with a dedicated SEO or data function, this is an advantage. For teams without that specialization, the learning curve adds onboarding time and may slow adoption. For stakeholder sharing, HubSpot AEO benefits from its existing reporting infrastructure— users can share dashboards across the platform without additional export steps.

Profound supports CSV exports and API-based reporting, but teams must configure additional steps to fit its standard stakeholder workflows.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Actionability and Workflows

This is where the two tools diverge significantly for most teams.

HubSpot AEO connects AI visibility data to content and campaign execution inside a single platform. When the tool identifies a prompt in which a brand is missing from AI-generated answers, it surfaces a prioritized recommendation. It provides a direct path to creating or updating the relevant content.

Marketing Hub and Content Hub handle the execution. Smart CRM provides audience context so that recommendations align with the segments and lifecycle stages that matter to the business. The result is a shorter cycle between identifying an AI visibility gap and publishing something to address it.

Profound provides improvement recommendations and an “Improve” module with tools like FAQ generation based on tracked prompts. But it lacks a built-in content execution layer. Acting on Profound’s insights requires taking them into a separate CMS, briefing a content team, and managing the production workflow externally.

For teams with dedicated content operations, this is manageable. For teams where the analyst and the content creator are the same person, or where speed to execution matters, it adds friction that compounds over time.

The transition from insight to execution is a critical operational challenge in AI SEO. Tracking visibility is relatively straightforward. Turning that data into a consistent publishing cadence is the harder operational problem, and it is the one HubSpot AEO is structurally designed to solve.

We like HubSpot AEO because CRM-informed recommendations enable the platform to prioritize visibility gaps based on real audience data rather than generic prompt volume. Teams can see which prompts matter to their actual buyer segments before deciding where to invest optimization effort.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Data Depth and Intelligence

Profound has the advantage in raw data depth. It tracks a larger set of AI platforms at the base edition (including Google AI Overviews and Claude), offers more flexible custom prompt configuration, and provides more granular insight into brand perception, such as how AI systems describe a brand, which sources influence those descriptions, and how positioning shifts across prompts and competitors over time.

For enterprise brand, PR, and data teams that need to audit AI-generated narratives or investigate why competitors are being cited more frequently, Profound provides deeper datA on sources, sentiment, and brand perception.

HubSpot AEO tracks AI visibility reliably across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, with daily updates, historical trend dashboards, and citation analysis. The data is structured for clarity over complexity, making it useful for teams that need to prioritize and act, rather than investigate in depth.

The platform’s citation tracking identifies which sources and content types drive AI answers, which is sufficient for most content optimization decisions.

The trade-off is clear: Profound offers more data; HubSpot AEO makes the data easier to act on. For most marketing and RevOps teams, the actionability advantage outweighs the analytical depth advantage. For enterprise teams with the resources to support deep analysis, Profound’s data layer adds strategic value.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Integrations and Ecosystem

HubSpot AEO’s integration advantage is structural. Because it is built into the HubSpot platform, AI visibility data connects natively to CRM records, campaign workflows, contact segments, and content tools.

HubSpot AEO requires no API setup, middleware, or additional configuration to route insights into execution. For teams already operating in HubSpot, this is a significant compounding advantage because AEO becomes another data source within a system they already use, rather than a separate tool that requires its own workflow.

Profound offers API access for custom integrations and connects with external CMS and marketing platforms, making it a flexible option for enterprise teams with established data infrastructure. The trade-off is that Profound’s flexibility requires technical setup and ongoing maintenance, adding operational complexity that HubSpot AEO avoids.

Profound fits well into custom stacks but does not provide pre-built execution workflows.

For teams evaluating both tools through a competitive intelligence lens, integration typically becomes the deciding factor—teams should ask where they already operate and which tool reduces the distance between insight and implementation.

HubSpot AEO vs. Profound Use Cases and Decision Framework

Choose HubSpot AEO if:

  • The team needs to move from AI visibility insight to content execution quickly
  • Marketing, SEO, content, and RevOps are working from a shared platform
  • Budget accessibility and ease of adoption are priorities
  • The team is already in HubSpot or evaluating it as a CRM and marketing platform

Choose Profound if:

  • The team has a dedicated SEO, brand, or data function with capacity for deep analysis
  • Brand perception, sentiment monitoring, and competitive narrative analysis are strategic priorities
  • API access or custom integrations with an existing data stack are required
  • Enterprise governance, SSO, and multi-platform AI tracking (including Google AI Overviews) are needed

Best for execution-focused teams: HubSpot AEO

Best for analysis-focused enterprises: Profound

Can I use both tools together?

Yes, and some enterprise teams do. Profound’s depth of analysis informs the strategic framing, including how AI systems describe a brand, which sources are most influential, and where competitive positioning is weakest.

HubSpot AEO then handles the execution layer: turning those insights into content updates, campaign triggers, and CRM-aligned optimization priorities.

In practice, most teams only need one platform, depending on whether their primary bottleneck is execution or analysis. If the primary challenge is acting on AI visibility data rather than analyzing it, HubSpot AEO covers the full workflow. If deep brand perception analysis is a standalone priority, particularly for large brands managing complex AI narratives across many platforms, Profound adds value that HubSpot AEO does not replicate.

Free Options for AEO and How to Start Fast

The HubSpot AEO Grader is the fastest way to establish an AI search visibility baseline without a subscription. It generates a 0–100 composite score across sentiment, presence quality, recognition, share of voice, and market position for ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. The Grader is a one-time diagnostic.

The AEO Grader does not provide continuous monitoring or custom prompt tracking, but it is the right first step for any team that has not yet measured its AI visibility.

Once a team has its baseline score, the decision about ongoing monitoring becomes clearer. If visibility gaps are significant and the team has the capacity to act on them, moving into HubSpot AEO’s paid monitoring and execution edition creates a repeatable improvement cycle.

If the team’s primary need is deeper analysis before committing to an optimization strategy, Profound’s free report also provides a useful starting point. Many teams skip the baseline step and move directly to paid platforms.

Teams should start with the Grader, define the workflow, and then scale into the tool that fits the team’s operating model.

Pro tip: Use the AEO Grader to benchmark a competitor before starting a paid trial. It takes under five minutes and surfaces a competitive context that sharpens the prompts worth tracking in any ongoing platform.

Frequently Asked Questions About HubSpot AEO vs. Profound

Do I need a HubSpot subscription to use AEO?

No. HubSpot AEO is available as a standalone product at $45 per month (billed annually) and does not require an existing HubSpot subscription. The free AEO Grader also requires no subscription. Teams that want to connect AEO recommendations to content workflows and CRM data will benefit from Marketing Hub, but it is not a prerequisite for accessing the core AEO product.

Can I run a one-time analysis before I commit?

Yes. Both tools offer free entry points. The HubSpot AEO Grader generates a one-time brand visibility score across major answer engines at no cost. Profound offers a free one-time AEO report.

Both AEO Grader and Profound’s free report require no credit card. Use these diagnostics to establish a baseline and evaluate which platform’s output is most useful for the team’s workflow before committing to a paid plan.

When should I use both HubSpot AEO and Profound together?

Using both makes sense for enterprise teams where separate functions handle brand perception analysis and content execution. Profound can serve as the strategic intelligence layer for SEO or brand teams that need deep citation and sentiment analysis.

HubSpot AEO can serve as the execution layer for marketing and content teams acting on those insights. For most teams, one platform is sufficient, but the choice depends on whether execution or analysis is the primary bottleneck.

How do I measure impact across channels?

AI visibility metrics are indicators, not direct pipeline measures. Leverage them as a research and prioritization layer in tandem with conversion, data, Google Search Console data, and sales feedback.

In HubSpot AEO, historical trend dashboards enable tracking of visibility changes over time and their correlation with content updates. To measure meaningfully, teams must record when changes are made, compare periods, and link visibility shifts to downstream signals such as organic traffic, lead quality, or assisted conversions— not treat score improvements as standalone success metrics.

item.title: Ahrefs Brand Radar alternatives for marketing teams
item.description: G2’s 2026 Answer Economy research found that 51% of B2B software buyers start their research with an AI chatbot more often than Google. That shift means marketing teams need to track not only traditional search performance but also how AI assistants and answer engines mention, cite, and recommend brands.
item.content:encoded:
G2’s 2026 Answer Economy research found that 51% of B2B software buyers start their research with an AI chatbot more often than Google. That shift means marketing teams need to track not only traditional search performance but also how AI assistants and answer engines mention, cite, and recommend brands.

HubSpot AEO is one option for continuous tracking and prioritized recommendations, while HubSpot’s free AI Search Grader provides a one-time baseline. HubSpot’s guide to AI-powered brand tracking offers additional context for teams building a broader measurement program.

This guide compares six Ahrefs Brand Radar alternatives for marketing teams that need a different mix of AI model coverage, evidence, integrations, pricing, and rollout fit. It also explains how to connect AI visibility with content performance, pipeline, and broader AI marketing analytics.

Why Marketers are Considering Ahrefs Brand Radar Alternatives Now

Ahrefs is an SEO platform for backlink analysis, keyword research, rank tracking, site audits, competitive research, and AI visibility. Ahrefs Brand Radar now tracks brand mentions and citations across major AI answer engines. It supports custom prompt monitoring, so teams comparing alternatives should evaluate its fit with their current workflow rather than assume Ahrefs lacks conversational AI tracking.

Marketers may still choose another AI visibility tool when they need a different mix of model coverage, prompt-level detail, integrations, evidence, pricing, or reporting workflows. HubSpot AEO is one alternative for teams that want ongoing visibility tracking alongside prioritized recommendations.

1. They needed more granular data.

Large marketplaces can need more prompt-level context and reporting flexibility than a broad visibility score provides. Alexandra Novikava, a marketer at Truck1, describes her team’s experience:

“At first, we used Ahrefs Brand Radar to observe what sorts of references were being made to us by AI engines but have now transitioned toward custom API tracking and alternative SEO intelligence tools,” Novikava explains.

Novikava says Truck1 needed more detail about the queries where competitors gained visibility and greater flexibility in its data-collection workflow. Ahrefs has since added custom prompt tracking with configurable models, locations, and tracking frequencies, so teams should compare the level of detail they need with Brand Radar’s current capabilities.

2. They wanted prompt-specific tracking.

In specialized B2B markets, one high-intent prompt can matter more than a broad brand-mention count. Colleen Barry, head of marketing at Ketch, puts it plainly:

“In B2B, one mention in the right context matters more than ten generic mentions,” Barry explains.

Ketch adopted Ahrefs Brand Radar in early 2025 to establish an initial baseline for AI-search visibility. Barry’s team later wanted more control over industry-specific prompt libraries so it could evaluate how conversational engines handled nuanced privacy and compliance queries and determine whether thought-leadership content influenced those responses.

Ahrefs now supports custom prompts, so Ketch’s experience should be read as a historical workflow-fit decision rather than evidence that Brand Radar currently cannot track specific prompts.

3. They looked for a lower-cost fit.

Pricing can become the deciding factor when teams compare AI visibility tools. This was Ashot Nanayan’s experience as founder and CEO of B2BSEO. During Brand Radar’s open beta, Nanayan estimated that the Ahrefs subscription and AI-monitoring add-ons his team needed would have cost about $800 per month. He also wanted localized prompt customization and broader model coverage at the time.

Ahrefs’ packaging has changed since that experience. Standalone Brand Radar currently starts at $199 per month for a single platform, while separate custom-prompt packages start at $50 per month. Nanayan ultimately preferred a dedicated AI visibility platform that offered broader coverage and a lower overall cost for his team’s use case.

4. They needed stronger links between visibility and customer actions.

For Matthew Kinneman, founder of Bully Max, Ahrefs Brand Radar provided a useful starting point for understanding how AI-search platforms referenced the brand. His team moved toward a broader measurement approach because visibility alone did not show whether AI mentions aligned with traffic, engagement, or conversions.

As Kinneman explains, “the biggest lesson for me was that AI visibility is only valuable if you can tie it back to actions customers take afterward. Otherwise, it’s easy to end up optimizing for a metric that looks good but doesn’t drive business growth.”

Today, Bully Max combines multiple data sources to evaluate AI-driven discovery alongside traditional search performance and customer behavior. Rather than treating AI visibility as a standalone KPI, Kinneman argues that teams should evaluate it within the context of the entire customer journey.

His experience reflects one of the most important criteria for evaluating Ahrefs Brand Radar alternatives: marketing teams need to connect AI visibility with CRM, attribution, pipeline, and revenue reporting. HubSpot AEO is one example of a product built around that broader measurement workflow.

Ahrefs Alternatives at a Glance

Bonus diagnostic: HubSpot’s free AI Search Grader provides a one-time baseline across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini before a team commits to ongoing tracking.

What Features Matter Most for AI Visibility Tools

AI visibility tools track brand mentions, citations, and recommendation patterns across AI assistants and AI-search surfaces. Unlike a traditional rank tracker, an AI visibility platform also needs to account for generated answers, preserve evidence, and show how results change over time.

The strongest Ahrefs Brand Radar alternatives should be evaluated on AI model coverage, data freshness, evidence quality, segmentation, integrations, pricing, and team fit.

AI Model Coverage and Data Freshness

Model coverage matters because buyers do not rely on a single answer engine. A tool that monitors several AI platforms gives teams a broader view of where a brand appears, while a single-engine tracker can make sense when one platform dominates a company’s audience or workflow.

Data freshness matters for a different reason: AI-generated answers change. Compare how frequently each tool reruns tracked prompts, whether cadence varies by plan or model, and how much historical data the product preserves. Daily data can be useful for active optimization, while weekly or monthly tracking may be enough for broader trend reporting.

LLM Visibility Tools That Support Segmenting by Persona or Journey

Aggregated visibility scores can hide where a brand is actually gaining or losing ground. Segmenting prompts by buyer persona or journey stage helps marketing teams distinguish broad awareness from high-intent consideration and purchase questions.

G2’s 2026 Answer Economy report found that 71% of B2B software buyers rely on AI chatbots at some point in their research process. That makes it useful to measure visibility at more than one stage of the buying journey.

  • Awareness stage: Track broad category and problem-oriented prompts, such as “How to automate B2B lead routing,” to see whether answer engines associate the brand with the problem it solves.
  • Consideration stage: Track comparison and shortlist prompts, such as “Top CRM systems for mid-market software companies,” to see which competitors answer engines group together and which sources influence those recommendations.
  • Decision stage: Track bottom-of-the-funnel prompts, such as “HubSpot vs. Livespace pricing and integrations,” to check whether answer engines return accurate, conversion-ready product information. In its own 2025 analysis, Ahrefs found that AI-search visitors converted at a 23x higher rate than traditional organic-search visitors for Ahrefs. Treat that as an Ahrefs-specific result, not a universal conversion benchmark.

Pro tip: Segmenting by persona prevents a strong aggregate score from hiding an important audience gap. High visibility among developers evaluating APIs, for example, does not mean the brand is equally visible to the marketing leaders who control budget.

AI Visibility Tool Integrations and Reporting

Integrations determine whether AI-search insights stay trapped in another dashboard or become part of a team’s existing reporting workflow. Useful platforms can connect AI visibility with CRM data, business intelligence, web analytics, marketing automation, or exportable data that teams can combine with broader AI marketing analytics.

Those connections matter because marketing teams eventually need to compare visibility with traffic, leads, pipeline, and revenue. HubSpot’s 2026 State of Marketing report found that 12.4% of marketers cite difficulty sharing data across their organization as a top challenge. Adding another disconnected measurement tool can make that problem worse.

Reporting quality matters just as much as the integration itself. Historical trends, exportable evidence, custom dashboards, and stakeholder-friendly summaries help teams understand whether changes in AI search engines coincide with changes in content performance and business outcomes.

Pro tip: Look for a tool that preserves historical AI visibility data rather than showing only the latest score. Products such as HubSpot AEO show visibility trends over time, which gives teams a more useful baseline for evaluating content, PR, and brand work.

Evidence Quality, Pricing, and Team Fit

A visibility score is much more useful when a team can inspect the evidence behind it. Look for products that preserve the underlying AI response, cited sources, timestamps, model information, or other records that make results auditable. That evidence can also strengthen competitive intelligence by showing which sources help competitors appear in recommendations.

Three practical questions can narrow the shortlist.

  • Evidence quality: Can the team inspect the response and citations behind a visibility score, or does the platform show only an aggregate metric?
  • Pricing and scale: How does cost change as the team adds prompts, models, locations, projects, users, or reporting frequency?
  • Team fit: Does the product support the workflows, permissions, exports, integrations, and reporting cadence that marketing, SEO, content, and revenue teams actually need?

A lower entry price does not automatically make one AI visibility tool a better fit. Compare the cost of the monitoring program the team will realistically run, not only the cheapest advertised plan.

Ahrefs Brand Radar Alternatives

1. HubSpot AEO

Source

HubSpot AEO is an AI visibility tool that tracks how a brand appears across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. It measures visibility and sentiment, compares competitor share of voice and citation sources, tracks buyer-relevant prompts, and turns visibility gaps into prioritized recommendations.

Standalone HubSpot AEO does not require a HubSpot subscription. Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise include AEO, where CRM data can inform prompt suggestions and recommendations and help teams connect AI visibility with pipeline and revenue.

Key Features

  • Brand visibility and sentiment: Tracks how frequently a brand appears for monitored prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini and shows the sentiment around those mentions.
  • Competitor and citation analysis: Compares competitor visibility and shows which domains and content AI engines cite, giving teams evidence they can use to prioritize content and outreach.
  • Prompt tracking and prioritized recommendations: Suggests relevant prompts, monitors them over time, and recommends specific actions based on visibility gaps.

Best for: Marketing teams that want ongoing AI visibility measurement plus a clear workflow for turning findings into content and campaign actions.

Pricing: $50 per month for 25 prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, or $45 per month with annual billing. HubSpot offers a 28-day free trial, and teams can purchase additional prompts.

What we like: HubSpot AEO combines measurement with an action layer. Instead of stopping at a visibility score, it shows where competitors are winning, what sources influence those answers, and what the team can do next.

What customers say: One customer success director writes in a G2 review, “I like the potential of HubSpot AEO to bring structure to how we understand and improve our discoverability. The ability to surface gaps in where we’re not being found — and recommend content to fill those gaps — is especially valuable, particularly when it can be filtered by audience or segment.”

Another reviewer writes in a G2 review, “I love the citation analysis in HubSpot AEO. Knowing exactly which domains and content AI engines cite when recommending software in our category has been a genuine game-changer for us. It moved AEO from something abstract we monitored to something we could actively build a strategy around.”

2. Profound

Source

Profound is an AEO platform built for teams that need detailed visibility analysis plus workflows for acting on that data. Its Answer Engine Insights product tracks how brands and competitors appear across AI platforms, while its Agents, Agent Analytics, and Prompt Volumes products extend the platform into content workflows, AI-sourced traffic analysis, and prompt research.

Its public plans range from ChatGPT-only monitoring to broader enterprise coverage, making Profound a stronger fit for organizations that expect AI visibility to become a dedicated program rather than an occasional reporting task.

Key Features

  • Answer Engine Insights: Tracks how a brand and its competitors appear in AI answers and preserves response-level visibility data.
  • Agent Analytics: Measures AI-sourced traffic and attribution across monitored domains and connects with analytics tools.
  • Agents and Prompt Volumes: Supports AEO content workflows and helps teams understand which topics and queries people are prompting in answer engines.

Best for: Larger companies and agencies building a dedicated AEO program that needs detailed reporting, broader model coverage, and enterprise controls.

Pricing: Profound pricing starts at $99 per month, billed yearly, for ChatGPT tracking and 50 prompts. Growth costs $399 per month, billed yearly, and includes three answer engines and 100 prompts. Enterprise uses custom pricing and can add up to nine answer engines.

What we like: Profound goes beyond a single visibility score. Its combination of response monitoring, AI-sourced traffic analysis, prompt research, and enterprise functionality gives teams several ways to build a broader AEO program.

3. Peec.ai

Source

Peec AI is an AI search analytics platform for tracking brand visibility, citations, competitors, and prompts across multiple AI models. Teams can organize prompts by project, compare performance over time, and examine the domains and URLs that appear in AI-generated responses.

Peec complements traditional AI SEO rather than replacing it. Its focus is the answer-engine layer: which brands appear, which sources get cited, and how those patterns change across tracked prompts.

Key Features

  • Multi-model visibility tracking: Public brand plans let teams choose three models and run tracked prompts daily.
  • Citation and competitor analysis: Shows cited domains and URLs alongside competitor visibility so teams can investigate why other brands appear.
  • Reporting and access: All public brand plans include unlimited users; Advanced adds multi-country reporting and Looker Studio, while Enterprise adds API access and SSO.

Best for: SEO and content teams that need broad AI model coverage, daily tracking, and collaborative access without pricing seats separately.

Pricing: Peec AI pricing starts at $95 per month for Starter with 50 prompts and one project. Pro costs $245 per month for 150 prompts and two projects. Advanced costs $495 per month for 350 prompts and five projects. Enterprise uses custom pricing.

What we like: Peec keeps public-plan user access unlimited while scaling primarily through prompts, projects, countries, and model requirements. That structure can make collaboration easier when SEO, content, and other stakeholders all need access to the same visibility data.

4. Xofu

Source

Xofu focuses on bottom-of-the-funnel and purchase-intent prompts — the questions buyers use to shortlist vendors, compare products, and evaluate solutions. It tracks recommendations over time and helps teams see which competitors appear, which sources support those recommendations, and where citation gaps exist.

That narrow focus distinguishes Xofu from broader brand-monitoring tools. It is designed around prompts that sit closer to a buying decision rather than every possible mention of a brand.

Key Features

  • Bottom-of-the-funnel prompt tracking: Monitors prompts such as “best X for Y,” vendor comparisons, and solution evaluations.
  • Competitive benchmarking: Shows which competitors appear for each tracked buyer prompt and how visibility changes over time.
  • Citation-gap analysis: Identifies the sources that answer engines cite when competitors appear so teams can prioritize content and off-site opportunities.

Best for: SaaS companies, consultants, and agencies that care most about AI visibility in commercial and purchase-intent prompts.

Pricing: Xofu pricing includes a free plan with 50 prompts per model and weekly reporting. Consultant costs $99 per month for 200 prompts per model and weekly reporting. Agency Weekly costs $499 per month for 500 prompts per model. Agency Daily costs $999 per month for 200 prompts per model and daily reporting.

What we like: Xofu keeps the analysis centered on the prompts that influence vendor selection. That makes its reports easier to connect with competitive positioning and pipeline questions than a broad visibility score alone.

5. Mangools AI Search Grader

Source

Mangools AI Search Grader is a free diagnostic tool that measures how a brand performs across AI-search models. It combines visibility and ranking into an AI Search Score and shows how the brand compares with competitors for automatically generated prompts.

Users can run the tool without an account using three supported models. A free Mangools account unlocks all seven supported models and additional searches.

Key Features

  • AI Search Score: Combines visibility, average ranking position, and model weighting into a score from 0 to 100.
  • Model-level results: Shows where a brand appears for analyzed prompts across multiple AI models.
  • Competitor benchmarking: Compares the brand with other companies that appear in the same generated results.

Best for: Marketers and SEO teams that want a free baseline before investing in continuous AI visibility monitoring.

Pricing: AI Search Grader is free. For continuous monitoring, Mangools offers the separate paid AI Search Watcher product.

What we like: The AI Search Score reduces several visibility and ranking signals to one easy-to-read benchmark while still letting users inspect the underlying model-level results.

6. Morningscore ChatGPT Rank Tracker

Source

Morningscore ChatGPT Rank Tracker monitors whether ChatGPT mentions or recommends a brand for selected prompts and shows the answer and source evidence behind each result. It sits inside Morningscore’s broader SEO platform, giving teams one place to work with traditional search metrics and ChatGPT visibility.

Its narrower engine focus is the main distinction from multi-model AI visibility platforms: the tracker centers on ChatGPT, and prompt lookups run weekly.

Key Features

  • ChatGPT prompt tracking: Monitors selected prompts on a weekly schedule.
  • Mention and citation evidence: Shows the actual ChatGPT answer and sources instead of reporting only an aggregate visibility score.
  • Competitor comparison: Helps teams compare which brands appear for the prompts they monitor.

Best for: Teams that primarily care about ChatGPT visibility and want that monitoring inside the same product they use for SEO.

Pricing: Morningscore pricing starts at $69 per month for Lite with 10 ChatGPT prompts. Business costs $99 per month for 100 prompts, Pro costs $159 per month for 500 prompts, and Premium costs $299 per month for 2,000 prompts. A 14-day free trial is available without a credit card.

What we like: Morningscore shows the underlying ChatGPT response and source evidence, which makes a reported mention easier to validate than a score alone.

Bonus: HubSpot AI Search Grader

Source

HubSpot AI Search Grader is a free, one-time diagnostic that checks how ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini represent a brand. It scores five dimensions — sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market competition — and returns a composite score with written interpretation.

The Grader serves a different purpose from paid HubSpot AEO. AI Search Grader answers “How do answer engines represent my brand right now?” while HubSpot AEO continuously tracks specific prompts, competitors, and changes over time.

Key Features

  • Five-dimension scoring: Measures sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market competition.
  • Cross-platform analysis: Runs the assessment across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini rather than relying on one answer engine.
  • Written interpretation: Explains the score and category results so marketers can understand what the numbers mean.

Best for: Marketing leaders, brand managers, SEO professionals, and content teams that want a free baseline before choosing a continuous AI visibility tool.

Pricing: Free. HubSpot describes AI Search Grader as a one-time check and says no account is required.

What we like: AI Search Grader makes a new measurement category easier to understand. The five-part score gives teams a simple starting point without requiring them to design a prompt-tracking program first.

The Answer Engine Report similarly calls its five-dimension scoring “the most pedagogically useful framework in the directory for explaining what AI visibility actually means to non-specialists.” The review also notes that the report is easier for marketing leaders to understand than many exhaustive practitioner dashboards.

Choosing an Ahrefs Brand Radar Alternative That Connects to Pipeline

AI visibility becomes more useful when teams can compare it with the metrics that already matter to the business: traffic, leads, opportunities, pipeline, and revenue. An AI visibility product does not need to function as a CRM. Still, its reporting workflow should make it possible to connect visibility trends with the systems marketing and sales teams already use.

The same principle applies to content ROI. Visibility data can show where a brand appears, but teams also need evidence that helps them identify which pages, topics, and sources may be contributing to those results and what they should work on next.

HubSpot’s integrated AEO experience in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise uses CRM data to surface prompts that are more relevant to actual buyers. HubSpot also positions that CRM-connected experience as a way to connect AI visibility with pipeline and revenue.

For teams using HubSpot, several products contribute to that workflow.

  • HubSpot Smart CRM: HubSpot’s AI-powered system of record gives marketing and sales teams shared customer context across contacts, deals, and attribution data.
  • Marketing Hub: AEO in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise can use CRM context to inform prompt tracking while marketing teams manage campaigns and reporting in the same platform.
  • Content Hub: Content teams can use visibility and citation findings to prioritize updates, strengthen topic coverage, and create content that addresses gaps surfaced by AEO analysis.

HubSpot AEO also provides prioritized recommendations rather than stopping at a visibility score. Those recommendations can point teams toward content updates, new pages, and citation opportunities based on where the brand is losing visibility.

That turns AI visibility into actionable competitive intelligence: teams can see what brands answer engines recommend, which sources shape those recommendations, and where the brand has an opportunity to improve.

Source

Ultimately, the best Ahrefs Brand Radar alternative depends on the outcome a team needs. Basic mention monitoring may be enough for an early-stage program. Teams that want to connect AI visibility with content performance, attribution, pipeline, and revenue should give more weight to reporting, integrations, evidence, and actionable recommendations.

How to Implement an Ahrefs Brand Radar Alternative

Implement an Ahrefs Brand Radar alternative as a controlled rollout: establish reporting, standardize prompts, validate results, preserve evidence, and test the workflow before expanding it. The goal is to add a repeatable AI visibility measurement layer alongside traditional search reporting, not to replace SEO measurement entirely.

Step 1: Set up integrations and reporting foundations.

Start by deciding where AI visibility data will live and how the team will compare it with existing marketing and revenue metrics.

  • Establish a shared taxonomy: Align prompt groups with the product lines, audience segments, journey stages, or reporting categories the team already uses.
  • Separate informational and commercial prompts: Keep broad awareness questions distinct from high-intent comparison and purchase prompts so one aggregate score does not blur different objectives.
  • Define the reporting destination: Decide whether the team will use the vendor dashboard, exports, an analytics tool, or a CRM-connected reporting workflow.

Step 2: Establish prompt governance.

Consistent prompts make trend data easier to interpret.

  • Use real buyer language: Build the tracking set around questions prospects actually ask rather than internal marketing terminology.
  • Document prompt changes: When comparability matters, keep prompts stable during a reporting period and record intentional edits so the team understands when a time series changes.
  • Assign ownership: Decide who can add, remove, or revise tracked prompts and how often the team reviews the library.

Step 3: Implement multi-run quality assurance.

Generated answers vary, so teams should not treat one response as definitive.

  • Repeat high-priority tests: Run important prompts more than once when the product and budget allow it.
  • Compare supported models and locations: Check whether a result persists across the answer engines or geographic settings that matter to the business.
  • Investigate outliers: Review the underlying answer and citation evidence before changing strategy because of a sudden visibility spike or drop.

Step 4: Build an evidence repository.

Keep enough evidence to explain what happened behind a visibility score.

  • Capture the underlying response: Save response text, screenshots, exports, or other evidence the platform provides.
  • Preserve citation information: Record the source URLs an answer engine cited, especially when a competitor gains or loses visibility.
  • Add context: Store the date, model, prompt, location, and other relevant settings so the team can reproduce or interpret the result later.

Step 5: Pilot, compare, and scale.

Test the workflow with a limited prompt set before rolling it out across every product, region, or audience.

  • Evaluate data quality: Determine whether the platform produces evidence the team trusts and can explain.
  • Measure operational fit: Compare reporting friction, integration needs, prompt limits, model coverage, and cost with the current workflow.
  • Scale what works: Expand the prompt set, teams, models, or locations only after the pilot establishes a useful baseline and a repeatable reporting process.

Frequently Asked Questions About Ahrefs Brand Radar Alternatives

How do I validate AI visibility data across different models?

Validate AI visibility data by running the same priority prompts more than once and comparing outputs across the models, locations, and tracking frequencies the tool supports. Keep the underlying response and citation evidence so the team can confirm that a reported visibility score matches what the answer engine actually returned.

How long does it take to see results after switching tools?

A new tool can begin collecting baseline data as soon as tracking starts, but there is no universal four-to-six-week window for meaningful results. The time needed depends on the product’s tracking cadence, the stability of the prompt set, changes in the underlying answer engines, and how quickly content changes appear in generated responses.

Can I track brand visibility by region or persona?

Some AI visibility tools support geographic segmentation, persona-oriented prompt groups, or both, but capabilities vary by vendor and plan. Use location settings where the product supports them, and organize separate prompt groups around specific buyer roles or journey stages so the comparisons remain consistent.

What’s the best way to connect AI visibility to revenue?

Connect AI visibility to revenue by bringing visibility, referral traffic, CRM, and attribution data into the same reporting workflow. Compare changes in high-intent prompt visibility with qualified leads, influenced opportunities, and closed revenue, but avoid claiming causal impact when the data only shows a correlation.

Do I still need traditional SEO tools with an AI visibility tracker?

Yes. AI visibility trackers and traditional SEO tools answer different questions and work best together. AI visibility platforms show how brands appear in generated answers, while SEO tools measure rankings, backlinks, technical health, keyword opportunities, and organic traffic. For most marketing teams, AI visibility complements traditional SEO rather than replacing it.

Which Ahrefs Brand Radar alternative is right for your team?

Ahrefs Brand Radar is one of several ways to measure AI visibility. The six alternatives in this guide range from free diagnostics and ChatGPT-specific tracking to multi-model platforms built for ongoing reporting, evidence collection, and enterprise workflows. The right choice depends on the models a team needs to monitor, the evidence it needs to preserve, the integrations it relies on, and the cost of running the program at the required scale.

For teams that want continuous monitoring plus prioritized next steps, HubSpot AEO combines visibility, sentiment, competitor citation analysis, prompt tracking, and recommendations. Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise add CRM context for teams that want AI visibility to sit closer to their existing marketing and revenue reporting.

After reviewing these options, I think the biggest differentiator is whether the data gives a marketing team a clear next action and a credible way to connect visibility with business outcomes. A tool that only produces a score can answer “Are we visible?” A stronger workflow can also help answer “Why?” and “What should we do next?” That is the standard I would use when choosing an Ahrefs Brand Radar alternative.

item.description: If you’re comparing Scrunch alternatives, start by separating monitoring from execution. Monitoring tools show how brands appear in AI-generated answers. Optimization tools add recommendations, content briefs, or workflows that help teams act on those findings.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re comparing Scrunch alternatives, start by separating monitoring from execution. Monitoring tools show how brands appear in AI-generated answers. Optimization tools add recommendations, content briefs, or workflows that help teams act on those findings.

Answer engine optimization (AEO) has become a budget priority. In Conductor’s 2026 survey of more than 250 enterprise digital leaders, 94% planned to increase AEO investment.

This guide compares 13 Scrunch AI competitors by use case, engine coverage, execution features, pricing, seat limits, and customer relationship management (CRM) integration.

Why Teams Are Comparing Scrunch Alternatives Now

Scrunch is an AI search visibility and agent experience platform. Its Core plan tracks 125 prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Microsoft Copilot. Core also includes five monthly site audits, insights and recommendations, one monthly page optimization, basic content generation, and five user licenses. Teams may still compare alternatives for four practical reasons.

  • Entry price: Core costs $250 per month, which may exceed the budget for an early AEO pilot.
  • Engine coverage: Core covers four platforms. Teams that need Gemini, Claude, Google AI Mode, Grok, or Meta AI need Enterprise or another product.
  • Execution depth: Core includes recommendations and limited optimization support, but teams that need large-scale content creation or automated workflows may need a stronger execution layer.
  • Packaging and scale: Core limits teams to 125 prompts, one brand workspace, and five users. Enterprise pricing is custom.

For teams that want visibility data connected to customer context and marketing workflows, HubSpot AEO is a practical first alternative to evaluate.

Scrunch Alternatives at a Glance

Scrunch alternatives differ most in starting price, engine coverage, execution support, seat access, and workflow integration. The table below reflects publicly available pricing and packaging as of July 2026.

Best Scrunch Alternatives By Use Case

1. HubSpot AEO: Best Overall

HubSpot AEO tracks brand visibility, sentiment, competitor share of voice, prompts, and citations across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. It also turns visibility findings into prioritized recommendations.

The stand-alone product does not require another HubSpot subscription. Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise add connected CRM context, content creation, and campaign workflows.

Key Features

  • Prompt suggestions: HubSpot recommends prompts from company, competitor, and industry context. Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise can also use CRM data to tailor those suggestions.
  • Competitor and citation analysis: The tool shows where competitors appear, which pages and domains earn citations, and where your brand is absent.
  • Prioritized recommendations: HubSpot translates visibility gaps into actions such as creating content, updating a page, addressing a technical issue, or pursuing an external citation.

Best for: Marketing teams that want AI visibility monitoring, recommendations, and content workflows connected in one system.

Pricing: HubSpot AEO includes a free 28-day trial with 25 free prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. After the trial, it costs $50 per month or $45 per month with annual billing. AEO is also included in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise.

What we like: The connection between customer context and content intelligence gives teams a clearer path from a visibility gap to a marketing action. The $50 stand-alone plan also lowers the cost of testing the category.

What the experts say: Sunil Manjunath, co-founder of Techhoor, said, “AEO differs from other GEO tools in that it knows all about your business already. GEO tools typically start slow with no knowledge of your business or how your customers search for you. However, HubSpot can pull from the CRM data that HubSpot already has related to customers to provide prompts and assist in generating the best content for your customers, compared to many of its competitors.”

Pro tip: If you use Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, check your account before buying a separate AEO subscription because AEO is already included.

Before you pay for another platform, run the free AI Search Grader. It provides a one-time analysis of how ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini represent your brand across sentiment, presence quality, brand recognition, share of voice, and market position.

2. GetMint: Best for Content Teams

Source

GetMint combines AI-driven visibility analysis with a GEO agent and content creation tools. Its Starter plan tracks 50 prompts across two topics, refreshes the data daily, and includes credits to create or optimize one content item each month.

The product focuses on moving teams from visibility findings into recommendations and content work rather than leaving the analysis in a stand-alone dashboard.

Key Features

  • Visibility analysis: Track prompts, citations, sentiment, and competitors across supported AI models.
  • GEO agent: Turn visibility gaps into recommended actions instead of stopping at the report.
  • Content creation and optimization: Create or improve content from GetMint’s findings, including pages affected by overlapping coverage or keyword cannibalization.

Best for: Content strategists and writers who want visibility data connected to content production.

Pricing: Starter costs $99 per month or $80 per month with annual billing. Growth costs $399 per month or $349 per month with annual billing. Enterprise and agency pricing is custom.

What we like: GetMint connects diagnosis to execution in a workflow that content teams can use without adding a separate optimization product.

What the experts say: Manjunath also said, “One thing I like about GetMint is that it allows you to identify and close gaps with its integrated content studio. If you want to find a solution for fixing your visibility issues rather than creating reports about them, then GetMint will be worth your time.”

3. Profound: Best for Enterprise Analytics

Source

Profound combines AI visibility analytics, agent analytics, and automated AEO work. Starter tracks 50 prompts in ChatGPT and includes 100 monthly credits for Profound Agents.

Growth expands coverage to ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. It includes 100 prompts, 9,000 analyzed responses per month, three seats, 400 agent credits, and all-time history.

Key Features

  • Answer Engine Insights: Measure brand mentions, citations, sentiment, and competitor share of voice.
  • Profound Agents: Generate or optimize content through credit-based agents.
  • Historical and enterprise reporting: Use all-time history, exports, integrations, and broader engine coverage on eligible plans.

Best for: Enterprise teams that need historical data, executive reporting, higher prompt volume, and automation.

Pricing: Starter costs $99 per month, billed annually. Growth costs $399 per month, billed annually. Enterprise pricing is custom.

What we like: Profound pairs deep reporting with an execution layer. Teams should note that broader engine coverage, three seats, and all-time history begin with Growth.

What the experts say: Jon Clark, managing partner at Moving Traffic Media, said, “Profound’s direct pipeline access to prompts across LLMs gives them the best visibility and competitive share-of-voice tracking I have found. We use it almost exclusively for baselining new AEO projects and for business development when there is an opportunity to show a potential client where they have opportunities versus where they stand today.”

4. AthenaHQ: Best for Automation

Source

AthenaHQ combines multi-model visibility monitoring with recommendations and automated content actions. Its free Essential plan includes 300 credits, five models, unlimited members, prompt and response analysis, source and competitor insights, content recommendations, and an AI agent.

Starter expands coverage to nine models and adds integrations, CSV exports, on-page and off-page actions, and a content optimization agent.

Key Features

  • Multi-model monitoring: Starter tracks visibility across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Grok, and additional models.
  • Content and optimization agents: AthenaHQ turns visibility gaps into on-page, off-page, and content actions.
  • Credit-based usage: One AI response consumes one credit, so teams must model usage across prompts, engines, and refresh frequency.

Best for: Teams that want to automate content optimization across many prompts and models.

Pricing: Essential is free and includes 300 credits. Starter costs $295 per month and includes 3,600 credits. Enterprise pricing is custom.

What we like: AthenaHQ gives teams a free entry point and includes unlimited members. Starter adds broader engine coverage and a more substantial execution workflow.

5. Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit: Best for Stack Consolidation

Source

Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit adds AI search monitoring to Semrush’s broader data environment. The Base plan tracks 25 custom prompts for one domain and reports mentions across ChatGPT, Google AI, Gemini, and Perplexity.

It also includes competitor research, prompt research, and an AI-readiness site audit, providing SEO teams with a way to compare AI visibility against their existing search data.

Key Features

  • Visibility reporting: Track mentions, rankings, sentiment, citations, and competitors.
  • Prompt and competitor research: Find prompts to monitor and compare brand performance with competing domains.
  • AI-readiness audit: Identify site issues that may limit AI visibility.

Best for: SEO teams that want AI visibility data beside keyword, backlink, audit, and content workflows.

Pricing: Base plan costs $99 per domain per month and is billed annually. It includes one domain and 25 custom prompts.

What we like: Teams already using Semrush can reduce tool sprawl by adding AI visibility research to a familiar environment. Buyers should still compare the one-domain and 25-prompt limits with stand-alone products.

What the experts say: Adam Binder, founder of Creative Click Media, said, “We’ve been using Semrush’s AI toolkit to better understand how our clients appear across AI-powered search platforms, and I love how it gives us a clear, easy-to-understand picture of where they stand in the rapidly changing world of AI search. Instead of guessing how AI platforms are sourcing and surfacing information, we can actually measure visibility and identify gaps.”

6. ZipTie: Best for Actionable Optimization

Source

ZipTie pairs AI visibility monitoring with data summaries and content optimizations. Its Basic plan includes 500 AI search checks per month across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity.

Basic also includes five AI data summaries and 10 content optimizations, giving teams a direct route from monitoring to action.

Key Features

  • Multi-engine tracking: Monitor visibility across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity.
  • AI data summaries: Convert visibility data into concise interpretations for teams and stakeholders.
  • Content optimizations: Use platform recommendations to improve pages connected to visibility gaps.

Best for: Teams that want optimization guidance inside the product they use for AI visibility monitoring.

Pricing: Basic costs $69 per month and includes 500 AI search checks, one seat, five data summaries, and 10 content optimizations. ZipTie offers a 14-day free trial.

What we like: ZipTie publishes clear usage limits and creates a direct path from monitoring to action. Teams should account for Basic’s three-engine and one-seat limits.

7. AirOps: Best for Content Operations at Scale

Source

AirOps combines AI search visibility insights with content refresh, creation, and distribution workflows. Its free Solo plan tracks 100 prompts and pages in ChatGPT, provides monthly opportunity reports, and includes 20,000 content-production tasks.

Paid plans add multi-engine insights, more frequent reports, integrations, team access, and scaled content workflows.

Key Features

  • AI visibility insights: Identify brand and content opportunities across tracked prompts and pages.
  • Content workflows: Refresh, create, and distribute content through repeatable workflows.
  • Platform integrations: Connect workflows to content management, SEO, AEO, social, and project-management products.

Best for: Content operations teams that want AI visibility findings connected to large-scale content production.

Pricing: Solo starts at $0 and includes one user. AirOps does not publish a numerical Pro price. Enterprise pricing is custom.

What we like: AirOps closes the distance between visibility research and content execution. Teams can begin with a free ChatGPT-only monitoring plan and move into broader engines and workflows as their program grows.

What the experts say: Nikolay Krastev, an SEO consultant, said, “The strength is that it isn’t a single-purpose AI tool—it’s a workflow builder that lets you chain AI calls, data sources, and outputs into repeatable production pipelines, which is exactly what serious AI search work requires. For content and AI-visibility workflows at scale, it gives you the kind of orchestration most teams try to hack together in Zapier or Make and never quite finish.”

8. Peec AI: Best for Reporting

Source

Peec AI focuses on daily AI visibility reporting for brands and agencies. Its Starter plan tracks 50 prompts across three selected models for one project and includes unlimited users.

Higher tiers add prompts, projects, countries, historical data, and reporting integrations, giving teams room to expand without changing products.

Key Features

  • Visibility and competitor tracking: Compare brand mentions, positions, and share of voice across selected AI models.
  • Source and citation analysis: Identify which domains and pages influence AI-generated answers.
  • Stakeholder reporting: Create readable reports and, on eligible plans, connect data to Looker Studio.

Best for: Teams that need clean, shareable AI visibility reports for stakeholders or clients.

Pricing: Starter costs $95 per month, Pro costs $245 per month, and Advanced costs $495 per month.

What we like: Peec AI combines clear reporting with unlimited users on the Starter plan, making collaboration easier for growing teams.

What the experts say: Douglas J. Darroch, managing director at Renaissance Digital Marketing, uses Peec AI as a primary AI search visibility tracker for client work. Darroch said, “What we like the most is the source and citation insights. It doesn’t just tell you whether a brand shows up in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews … it shows which sources those models are actually pulling from, so we can prioritize where to earn mentions. The competitor benchmarking and share-of-voice view also make it easy to show clients exactly where they rank against competitors in AI answers. We pair it with our own GA4 analytics review, but it’s become a core part of how we run GEO.”

9. Ahrefs Brand Radar: Best for Ahrefs Users

Source

Ahrefs Brand Radar combines a large search-backed prompt index with custom prompt tracking and citation research. Teams can investigate brands, products, regions, and people across AI platforms and connected discovery channels.

The product supports both broad market research and narrower tracking of the prompts that matter to an individual brand.

Key Features

  • Large prompt index: Research brand visibility across Ahrefs’ existing database of AI questions and answers.
  • Custom prompts: Track selected prompts repeatedly through a separate custom-prompt package.
  • Citation and competitor research: Identify cited domains, pages, brands, and competitive visibility patterns.

Best for: Ahrefs customers and data-heavy teams that want broad discovery research alongside custom AI prompt tracking.

Pricing: Access to one AI platform costs $199 per month. Access to all AI platforms costs $699 per month, and custom prompt packages start at $50 per month.

What we like: Brand Radar supports both high-level market research and targeted prompt monitoring. Its Ahrefs data environment will feel familiar to existing users, but buyers should budget for its separate subscription.

What the experts say: Jeremy Moser, co-founder and CEO of uSERP, said, “I’ve tested a ton of AI search visibility tools in my line of work, but I definitely recommend Ahrefs’ Brand Radar. It helps you track the intent behind these prompts and understand why different source materials are cited. From there, you can reverse engineer your strategy to build consensus across every touch point that matters: your website (content marketing), third-party sites (link building), directories (off-page SEO), social/forums (off-page).”

10. Rankshift: Best for Agencies

Source

Rankshift combines AI prompt tracking with content briefs, AI writing, crawler analytics, and reporting. Starter includes unlimited projects and seats, 150 prompts per day, 9,500 credits, and daily or weekly refresh options.

The product’s unlimited-project structure lets agencies divide their allowance across client accounts without purchasing a separate seat for every collaborator.

Key Features

  • Multi-client tracking: Manage unlimited projects and users within the plan’s credit allowance.
  • Content execution: Turn visibility findings into briefs and AI-assisted content.
  • Crawler and reporting tools: Analyze AI crawler activity and connect reporting through Looker Studio, APIs, and Model Context Protocol tools.

Best for: Agencies that need flexible project and seat access across multiple client accounts.

Pricing: Starter costs 69 euros per month, billed annually, and includes a 30-day trial.

What we like: Rankshift publishes its credit allowance and includes unlimited projects and seats. Agencies should still model credit use because consumption varies by model and refresh frequency.

11. SE Visible by SE Ranking: Best for Full-Stack SEO Plus AI

Source

SE Visible is SE Ranking’s stand-alone AI visibility product. Basic tracks 200 prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, analyzes about 12,000 answers per month, and supports three projects.

Teams that use the broader SE Ranking platform can instead buy its separate AI Search add-on, which includes access to SE Visible under a different usage model.

Key Features

  • Multi-engine monitoring: Track brand visibility across five major AI search environments.
  • Sentiment and citation analysis: Review brand sentiment, cited sources, answer text, and competitor performance.
  • Reporting and projects: Organize tracking across three projects and build reports for teams or clients.

Best for: SEO teams that want a stand-alone AI visibility product with the option to connect it to a broader SEO suite.

Pricing: SE Visible Basic costs $99 per month and includes a 10-day free trial. The separate SE Ranking AI Search add-on costs $89 per month for 200 checks.

What we like: SE Ranking offers buyers two options: a stand-alone visibility product or an add-on within its broader SEO software. Teams should compare the prompt-based and check-based allowances before making a choice.

12. OtterlyAI: Best for Budget Starters

Source

OtterlyAI is a lower-cost entry point for daily brand visibility tracking. Lite tracks 15 prompts across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Microsoft Copilot and includes unlimited team members.

Gemini, Google AI Mode, and Claude are available as paid engine add-ons, so teams should include those costs when comparing broader coverage.

Key Features

  • Brand visibility tracking: Monitor mentions, positions, sentiment, and competitors across supported AI search products.
  • GEO audit: Review a site’s readiness and identify opportunities that may affect AI visibility.
  • Prompt and citation research: Examine answers and cited sources for the prompts that matter to the brand.

Best for: Small teams and solo marketers that want accessible daily monitoring before committing to a higher-priced platform.

Pricing: Lite costs $29 per month. Annual billing reduces the subscription price by 15%.

What we like: OtterlyAI publishes clear entry limits and keeps the base price low. Buyers who need Gemini, Google AI Mode, or Claude should include the add-on costs in their comparison.

What the experts say: Chris Burdick, senior SEO consultant at Apiary Digital, told me, “Otterly is the tool I keep coming back to for AI search visibility monitoring. The interface is straightforward: you set up your brand and competitor terms, and it tracks how often and how accurately they appear in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other AI engines — which matters a lot when you’re trying to understand whether your content is actually influencing AI-generated answers.”

How to Test Scrunch Alternatives

Most teams begin evaluating an AI visibility tool with a demo or a short trial, much as they would evaluate other AI marketing tools. That approach can show you the interface and basic output, but it may not reveal how well the product fits your team’s operating rhythm.

Run a 30-day pilot when the vendor and your procurement timeline allow it. During the pilot, measure five things:

  • Coverage. Does the tool track the AI engines your buyers use? At minimum, compare ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Add Claude, Google AI Mode, or Microsoft Copilot when those environments matter to your audience.
  • Execution speed. How quickly can your team move from a finding to an action? Compare monitoring reports with recommendations, briefs, automated workflows, and technical guidance, including guidance on reducing page weight.
  • Content quality. If the tool generates briefs or recommendations, assess their specificity, factual accuracy, and usefulness rather than counting the number of suggestions.
  • Reporting clarity. Can a nontechnical stakeholder understand the output and the decision it supports without requiring an analyst to translate it?
  • Attribution readiness. Can you connect changes in AI visibility to traffic, leads, revenue, or another metric in your go-to-market strategy?

The central question is whether your team needs to know what is happening, act on it, or do both. Monitoring tools answer the first need. Execution tools add recommendations and workflows for the second.

Before the pilot begins, record the engines, prompts, competitors, regions, reporting cadence, and success criteria you will use. A consistent test plan produces a more useful comparison than evaluating each vendor with a different setup.

You can also run the free AI Search Grader to establish a one-time baseline before testing ongoing monitoring products.

Choosing the Right Scrunch Alternative for Your Team

Not all AI visibility tools solve the same problem. Choose a product based on the work your team must perform after receiving the data.

  • For reporting and enterprise analytics: Compare Scrunch, Profound, and Peec AI for visibility trends, competitor reporting, citations, and executive-ready analysis.
  • For monitoring plus execution: Compare HubSpot AEO, GetMint, AthenaHQ, ZipTie, and AirOps for recommendations, content actions, or automated workflows.
  • For stack consolidation: Compare Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit, Ahrefs Brand Radar, and SE Visible by SE Ranking when you want AI search data beside broader SEO work.
  • For a budget-conscious pilot: Compare HubSpot AEO’s free trial, AthenaHQ Essential, AirOps Solo, and OtterlyAI Lite.
  • For agency workflows: Compare Rankshift, Peec AI, and SE Visible based on project limits, user access, client reporting, and usage allowances.

My recommendation is to run the free AI Search Grader first. It provides a one-time snapshot of how ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini represent your brand. Use that analysis as a baseline, then test whether a paid product provides the ongoing monitoring, execution, and attribution workflow your team needs. For adjacent resources, explore HubSpot’s free content marketing tools.

Frequently Asked Questions About Scrunch Alternatives

Does Scrunch offer a free trial?

Scrunch offers a seven-day free trial of its Core plan. Core includes 125 prompts, five monthly site audits, one brand workspace, five user licenses, and four supported AI platforms.

HubSpot AEO offers a free 28-day trial with 25 prompts across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity.

Which Scrunch alternatives track Google AI Overviews?

Profound Growth, AthenaHQ, ZipTie, Peec AI, Ahrefs Brand Radar, Rankshift, SE Visible, and OtterlyAI explicitly list coverage of Google AI Overviews. Scrunch Core also tracks Google AI Overviews.

Coverage varies by plan. Confirm the exact engine list at the price point you intend to buy. HubSpot AEO currently tracks ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity rather than Google AI Overviews.

How long does switching from Scrunch take?

Switching time depends on the number of prompts, brands, competitors, regions, integrations, reports, and stakeholders involved. There is no reliable universal migration time.

Export or document your prompt taxonomy, rebuild the same tracking setup in the new product, and compare the two systems during the overlap period before canceling Scrunch. A two-week parallel run can provide a practical comparison, but it is an evaluation recommendation rather than a vendor benchmark.

What’s the difference between monitoring and optimization tools?

Monitoring tools collect and report data about brand visibility, sentiment, competitors, citations, and AI-generated answers. Optimization tools add recommendations, briefs, content creation, technical actions, or automated workflows.

Many current products combine both functions. Scrunch includes insights, recommendations, page optimization, and basic content generation, while HubSpot AEO, GetMint, AthenaHQ, ZipTie, and AirOps provide different forms of execution support alongside monitoring.

Which Scrunch alternative is best for agencies?

Rankshift is a strong agency option because Starter includes unlimited projects and users within a published credit allowance. Peec AI offers unlimited users on Starter and dedicated agency packages, while SE Visible supports multiple projects and client reporting.

The best choice depends on the number of clients, engines, prompts, refresh frequency, users, and reports the agency must support.

Can I use HubSpot AEO without a full HubSpot subscription?

Yes. HubSpot AEO is available as a stand-alone product for $50 per month or $45 per month with annual billing. A Marketing Hub subscription is not required.

AEO is also included in Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise for existing customers.

So, which tool should you choose?

The best Scrunch alternative depends on whether your team needs visibility data, execution support, enterprise analytics, or a consolidated marketing stack. Profound and Peec AI emphasize reporting; GetMint, AthenaHQ, ZipTie, and AirOps add distinct execution capabilities; Semrush, Ahrefs, and SE Visible suit teams that want AI search data alongside broader SEO work. HubSpot AEO stands out for teams that want prompt suggestions, recommendations, and content workflows connected to customer context.

I’ve been tracking this category closely since August 2025, and one pattern keeps becoming clearer: The most useful products show teams what to do next, not just where they stand. Start with the free AI Search Grader to establish a one-time baseline, then choose a paid product that supports the engines, workflows, limits, and attribution model your team can use consistently.
